angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 401,836 km at 93.98 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.6409 +/- 0.0152 mas (same row, RUWE 1.07): 93.98 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.5776 +/- 0.004 solar radii from Incha et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-417 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract): 401,836 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.569 +/- 0.012 solar masses from Incha et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-417 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3861 +/- 77 K from Incha et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-417 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Incha et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-417 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023MNRAS.523..474I/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-417.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.670, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
